claims.text: WHO Representative to Sudan Dr. Shible Sahbani reported more than 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 confirmed deaths, a case fatality rate of 13.7 percent, in an outbreak affecting several states, mainly in the western part of the country, the Darfurs and the Kordofans, briefing journalists in Geneva on 10 July 2026. Aid officials say the true number of fatalities is likely much higher, and the disease is expected to spread further as the rainy season sets in, particularly among people who have fled towns and rural areas in North Kordofan.

ECDC's cholera worldwide monthly overview and its Weekly Communicable Disease Threats Report (Week 33, 8-14 Aug 2026) both confirm the Sudan cholera dataset has not been refreshed since a data cut of 12 July 2026: 1,511 cumulative cases and 153 deaths reported since 1 January 2026, ranking Sudan second globally after DRC (3,841 cases). WHO/EMRO's dedicated Sudan crisis page returned repeated server errors (HTTP 502) and could not be verified this session.

UN News report (14 July 2026), citing OCHA, reconfirms WHO's count of 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 deaths as of 7 July 2026, and describes the outbreak's continued spread: new confirmed and suspected cases in Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur) and Tawila (North Darfur); West Kordofan reporting the highest caseload with new suspected cases and deaths; and North Kordofan reporting 32 new suspected cases in Gharb Bara locality in a single day. WHO delivered 8.5 tonnes of medical supplies to Kadugli and Dilling, South Kordofan — its first shipment there since December 2024 — and UNICEF delivered health supplies to El Fula, West Kordofan, serving about 429,000 people.

WFP report (data as of 17 July 2026): regular power outages are disrupting water supplies in El Obeid, and more than 30 new cholera cases have been recorded there as the city's displacement and hunger crisis deepens.

UN Women statement (24 July 2026): 'Cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July,' confirming no revised national cumulative total has superseded the 7 July WHO count as of this date.

WHO Multi-country outbreak of cholera, Epidemiological Update no. 38 (published 30 June 2026, data as of 31 May 2026): 'Sudan' is listed under the Eastern Mediterranean Region reporting 527 cumulative cholera cases and 61 deaths (CFR 11.6%) for 1 January to 31 May 2026, with 518 cases and 61 deaths (CFR 11.8%) in the preceding 28 days. This multi-country surveillance figure is dated to 31 May 2026 and is superseded chronologically by the 1,330-case/114-death figure WHO's Representative to Sudan reported on 10 July 2026 for the same national outbreak; re-checked 5 August 2026, no WHO or ReliefWeb Sudan-specific update newer than the 10 July figure has been published, and no allowlisted source has declared the outbreak contained.

ECDC's cholera-monthly page (updated 27 July 2026) reports for Sudan: 'Since 11 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 502 new cases, including 153 new deaths' and, year-to-date, 'Since 1 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 511 cases, including 153 deaths' — compared with 32,230 cases and 774 deaths in the equivalent 2025 timeframe (1 January-8 July 2025). This is a later data cutoff (12 July 2026) than WHO's Representative to Sudan's 10 July 2026 Geneva briefing figure (1,330 cases, 114 deaths) and is treated here as the most current published national aggregate.

description: Sudan's third cholera wave in as many years has spread since late June 2026 across war-affected western and central states, mainly the Darfurs and the Kordofans, where conflict and constrained humanitarian access hamper the response. ECDC's cholera-monthly surveillance (page updated 27 July 2026, data as of 12 July) records 1,511 cumulative cases including 153 deaths since 1 January 2026 -- the most current published national aggregate, superseding the more than 1,330 confirmed cases and 114 deaths WHO's Representative to Sudan reported on 10 July. WFP recorded more than 30 additional cases in El Obeid in mid-July as power outages disrupted the city's water supplies, and OCHA reporting describes spread into the Kalma/Kampala displacement camp in South Darfur, Tawila in North Darfur, and new localities in West and North Kordofan. WHO warns the outbreak could worsen as the rainy season sets in, aid officials say the true toll is likely higher, and the outbreak has not been declared contained.

impact.summary: ECDC's cholera-monthly surveillance reports 1,511 cumulative cholera cases including 153 deaths in Sudan since 1 January 2026, as of the 12 July 2026 data cut (implied case fatality rate ~10.1%) -- a dataset that had not been refreshed as of mid-August and that ranks Sudan second globally after DRC's 3,841 cases. The count supersedes the more than 1,330 confirmed cases and 114 deaths (CFR 13.7 percent) WHO reported on 10 July, in an outbreak centred on Darfur and Kordofan where WHO and UNICEF have scaled up medical supply deliveries to Kadugli, Dilling and El Fula. WFP recorded more than 30 cases in El Obeid alone in mid-July, and the outbreak has not been declared contained.
